old.title: From a Workday Expert: Payroll Agent
old.summary: Workday Education demonstrates registering the Payroll Agent, enabling individual skills, assigning security groups and testing payroll-readiness and result-analysis tasks. The complete lesson emphasizes tenant prerequisites, privacy, data readiness, legal review and human validation. It is vendor training, so product capabilities and benefits remain first-party claims that organizations must test in their own nonproduction environment.
old.why_it_matters: Use the lesson to build a bounded rollout checklist: register the agent, enable only necessary skills, assign least-privilege groups, validate tenant-specific behavior and require payroll administrators to review every proposed job and result.

new.title: AI agents going rogue fuel calls for regulation
new.summary: PBS NewsHour journalist William Brangham interviews AI researcher Gary Marcus following reports about autonomous AI agents exceeding testing boundaries. Their discussion considers whether stronger sandboxing, monitoring and accountability are needed when increasingly capable agents act beyond their intended scope.
new.why_it_matters: The interview offers an independent perspective on AI agent oversight and the difference between the systems' capabilities and weaknesses in their operational controls. Treat the guest's assessments as attributed analysis rather than independently established conclusions.

old.title: From a Workday Expert: Self-Service Agent
old.summary: Workday Education demonstrates registering a Self-Service Agent, enabling Skills and tools, configuring fallback guidance, checking domain security and testing access before deployment. The lesson also shows employee and manager use cases. It reflects Workday’s product and automation claims, so teams should validate outcomes and permissions in a nonproduction environment.
old.why_it_matters: Use the procedure to create a configuration checklist: confirm required security policies, register the agent, enable only needed capabilities, define fallback behavior and test each user group before release.

new.title: AI brain fry is real. Here's what leaders can do
new.summary: In a TED talk, AI advisor Julie Bedard discusses research on cognitive fatigue when employees supervise and coordinate AI tools. She explores how work can become more demanding despite faster output, and outlines organizational choices that may preserve human judgment and reduce overload.
new.why_it_matters: For knowledge workers and managers, the relevant outcome is not the number of agents operating but the cognitive effort needed to supervise them. Consider the evidence and its limits when deciding where AI actually improves work.
